To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the FNR of the thermophilic cyanbacterium, S. elongatus, is purified as three forms, the 45-kD, the 34- and the 78 kDa forms, and the association of the 45kDa form with phycocylanin via CpcDLike domain gives remarkable stability.
the FNR of a thermophilic Synechococcus species is composed of two domains, the CpcD phycobilisome-binding domain and the FNR catalytic domain.

the FNR from the thermophilic cyanbacterium Synechoccocus elongatus was purified to homogenity as three forms corresponding the 45-kD form retaining the CpdD-like domain, 34-kDa lacking the CpdD domain, and 78-kDa with phycocoyanin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification and characterization of the three forms of FNR in S. elongatus and the isolation of the petH gene encoding FNR.
the complete purification and characterization, and the gene cloning of FNR from the thermophilic cyanbacterium S. elongatus.
a novel FNR with a CpcD-like linker polypeptide domain and the association of FNR with phycobilisome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PetH gene encodes a 45-kDa FNR protein with a CpcD-like N-terminal domain in S. elongatus.
the PetH gene of S.elongatus encodes three different FNR forms, and these FNR forms are involved in a unique mechanism for the stabilization of FNR.
the 45-kD FNR is the native form of S. elongatu, which is a stable protein with high enzymatic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CpcD domain is a new type of protein domain which is found in the C-terminal regions of FNR and CpcD.
FNR in thermophilic cyanbacterium is a stable protein, but it is not so stable as to retain a phycocyanine-binding domain.
the CpcD domain of PetH in S. elongatus plays an important role in the assembly and/or stabilization of the phycobilisome and FNR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the association of FNR with phycobilisomes via CpcD is a common feature in cyanobacteria, and this interaction confers thermotolerance to the FNR.
the FNR in cyanobacteria is a multifunctional protein that is involved in the photosynthetic electron flow, the assembly of phycobilisomes, and the protection from proteolysis.
we have isolated the gene for the enzyme, FNR, from a thermophillic cyanobacterium and have shown that the enzyme can be isolated from this cyanobacterium as three forms.
